theater: 突尼斯城、比斯克拉灣與斯法克斯

battle.name: 法國入侵突尼斯
battle.theater: 突尼斯城、比斯克拉灣與斯法克斯
battle.brief: 一八八一年五月，法軍在突尼斯城登陸，貝伊同日簽下《巴爾多條約》，突尼斯自此淪為法國保護國；海上的事由比斯克拉灣的砲戰與加貝斯的封鎖包辦。卡面鐵甲艦生於一八六二年——英國那一代木殼包鐵的巨艦同年才在漢普頓路德灣互撼；開火的是法國的平鐵甲砲艇與老式巡洋艦，鐵甲艦的血緣到此已是末代。

kit.name: 鐵甲艦
kit.history: 木殼外面包了鐵。裝甲第一次比砲更難對付，砲塔的設計從此繞著它轉。

countries: 交戰一方是法蘭西第三共和國。陸軍方面臨時編成「突尼斯占領軍團」，由步兵營、獵兵、輕騎兵、工兵與野戰醫療隊組成，最初只投入三個營，進駐突尼斯城之後逐月擴充；指揮自成一套殖民戰爭的體系：總理茹費理在巴黎決定出兵，殖民部籌措軍費，外交部負責談判，海軍上將夏爾·德·多姆皮埃·多爾努瓦在海上指揮非洲海岸分艦隊，陸軍准將朱爾·布雷阿爾任占領軍團司令，民政一線交給常駐總督泰奥多爾·魯斯坦。另一方是突尼斯貝伊國：名義上仍是奧斯曼帝國的一個自治行省，國家元首是穆罕默德三世·阿薩迪克貝伊，軍隊稱「真主之軍」，是歷年裁減後剩下的數千殘兵，裝備以北非土砲與舊式火槍為主；另有無數由地方豪紳與部落首領率領的武裝民兵，遇戰即聚，散則務農。突尼斯一方的權力結構一端是貝伊宮廷，一端是控制清真寺學校的烏里瑪階層，首席謝赫哈達德·本·穆罕默德是精神上的領袖；而關稅與稅收自一八七四年起已由國際金融委員會接管，貝伊的財政命脈早被掐去一半。第三方是英國：官方嚴守中立，地中海艦隊駐紮馬爾他與蘇塞爾，司令希威特海軍上將卻公開致信支持法國出兵，倫敦輿論反對之下，英國既未出兵也未阻止。第四方是義大利：自居突尼斯的另一個宗主國，駐突代表朱塞佩·多西在義大利國會當眾抨擊法國，卻也沒有交戰。
countriesEn: One belligerent was the French Third Republic. On land an occupation corps for Tunisia was improvised out of infantry battalions, chasseurs, light cavalry, engineers and field medical units; only three battalions were committed at the outset, and the force was enlarged month by month after it entered the city of Tunis. Command followed the standard colonial pattern. Jules Ferry decided on the expedition in Paris, the colonial administration found the money, the foreign ministry handled the negotiation, Admiral Charles de Dompierre d'Hornoy commanded the squadron of the coast of Africa at sea, General Jules Bréart led the occupation corps on the ground, and civil government was handed to the resident-general Théodore Roustan. The other side was the Beylik of Tunis, nominally an autonomous province of the Ottoman Empire with the Bey Muhammad III as-Sadiq at its head. Its army, the Djund, was what remained of several thousand men after years of cuts, armed with North African bronze pieces and old muskets; alongside it stood the armed militias of local notables and tribal chiefs, who mustered for battle and returned to their fields in between. Power in Tunis ran on two tracks, the Bey's palace on one and the ulema who controlled the mosque schools on the other, with the chief Sheikh Haddad ben Mohamed its spiritual leader, and since 1874 the customs and taxes of the country had been in the hands of the international financial commission, so that half of the Bey's financial lifeblood was already gone. A third party was Britain: officially strict in its neutrality, with the Mediterranean Fleet based at Malta and Soueida Bay, yet its commander, Admiral Sir William Hewett, wrote openly to support the French expedition, and despite the uproar in London Britain neither fought nor intervened. A fourth was Italy, which claimed a share of the older suzerainty over Tunis: its consul in Tunis, Giuseppe Dossi, denounced the French action in the Italian parliament, but Italy did not go to war either.
people: 茹費理是整件事的推手：他在一八八一年以法國總理兼殖民部長的身分主導出兵，內閣開會拍板，議會於七月二日批准條約與經費，他在同年十一月二十七日因教育法案的爭議去職。海軍上將多爾努瓦是海上的全部：五月初率分艦隊抵達突尼斯港，隨後宣布封鎖拉古萊特、比斯克拉、斯法克斯、加貝斯與莫納斯提爾，是他把這場戰爭變成一場用艦隊解決的戰爭，也是他主張砲擊加貝斯並在該港建立封鎖的人。陸軍准將布雷阿爾是地面上的手：率三個營隨艦隊登陸，六月南下攻入斯法克斯，秋冬之間在薩赫勒地帶追剿起義兵，一八八二年一月進入加貝斯，至一八八二年中法軍在突尼斯的駐軍已增至兩萬五千人。外交上由外交部長舍爾曼-拉庫爾出面，最後通牒與《巴爾多條約》都經他的手，民政則由常駐總督魯斯坦接手，他其後出任駐土耳其大使。對面的核心人物是貝伊穆罕默德三世·阿薩迪克：他被迫簽下條約，交出外交與軍事的自主權，卻保住了王位與宮廷的虛名。真正不肯讓步的是烏里瑪：首席謝赫哈達德·本·穆罕默德在四月末的請願書上具名反對保護國，五月二十六日法國的最後通牒就是衝他而來，他隨即被捕囚禁，一八八一年九月被流放到利比亞的的黎波里，並於翌年二月死在流放地。地方豪紳穆罕默德·布齊德更早出手：一八八一年四月九日他當著貝伊與法國代表的面，在巴爾多宮遞上《陳情書》；事後他的兄弟在薩赫勒起兵，兵敗被捕流放，之後才獲赦免。義大利方面，駐突代表多西在三月三十日的國會演說中把法國的做法比作奧地利對丹麥的作為，義大利隨即派出鐵甲艦分隊到突尼斯港示威；而英國地中海艦隊司令希威特上將在四月致信支持法國行動，信件被公開後在倫敦引起一場外交風波。
peopleEn: Ferry was the man who pushed the whole thing. As prime minister and minister of colonies in 1881 he drove the expedition, the cabinet settled it, the chamber of deputies approved the treaty and the credits on 2 July, and he himself resigned that November over the school bill. Admiral de Dompierre d'Hornoy was everything that happened at sea: he brought his squadron into the roads of Tunis in early May, declared the blockade of La Goulette, Bizerte, Sfax, Gabès and Monastir, turned the campaign into a war settled by ships, and it was he who pressed for the bombardment of Gabès and for the blockade of that port. General Bréart was the hand on the ground: he landed three battalions with the squadron, drove south and entered Sfax in June, hunted the insurgents through the Sahel in the autumn and winter, moved into Gabès in January 1882, and by the middle of 1882 the French garrison in Tunisia had grown to some twenty-five thousand men. On the diplomatic side the foreign minister Challemel-Lacour conducted the ultimatum and the Bardo Treaty, while civil administration went to the resident-general Roustan, who afterwards became ambassador in Turkey. The central figure opposite was the Bey Muhammad III as-Sadiq, who was forced to sign away the independence of his country in foreign affairs and defence while keeping the title and the shadow of his palace. The ones who would not give way were the ulema: the chief Sheikh Haddad ben Mohamed signed the petition of late April against the protectorate, the ultimatum of 26 May was aimed straight at him, he was arrested and imprisoned, deported to Tripoli in Libya in September 1881, and died there in the following February. The local notable Mohamed Bouzid moved earlier: on 9 April 1881 he handed over the cahier de doléances in the Bardo palace before the Bey and the French representatives; afterwards his brothers rose in the Sahel, were beaten, captured and exiled, and only later pardoned. On the Italian side the consul Dossi compared French conduct in his parliamentary speech of 30 March to what Austria had done to Denmark, and Italy promptly sent a squadron of ironclads into the roads of Tunis as a display of strength; on the British side Admiral Hewett, commanding the Mediterranean Fleet, wrote in April to support the French action, and the publication of that letter set off a diplomatic storm in London.
kits: 卡面這件兵器是一八六二年定型的一代木殼包鐵戰艦——英國的砲塔從此繞著裝甲轉，正是在這一型上開始的。然而在一八八一年的突尼斯海灣，真正開火的是法國的平鐵甲砲艇米蘭號與塔日號：兩艘一八七〇年前後建造的低矮砲艇，各以兩門大後膛砲橫掃甲板，在比斯克拉灣與加貝斯外海的砲戰中都站在最前；法國海軍的木殼鐵甲主力艦此時已大部分列入預備或改裝，巡洋艦納伊克號、赫羅斯號、蒙塞居爾號與數艘魚雷砲艇、砲艇承擔封鎖線與偵察。鐵甲血統最重的體現者是義大利的分遣艦隊：法國造的木殼鐵甲艦卡洛·阿爾貝托號、恩里科·丹多洛號，以及英國桑穆達兄弟船廠建造的奧達斯號，這批船在一八八一年春夏駛入突尼斯港，是義大利的示強而不是作戰。守方的火力完全相反：比斯克拉與拉古萊特的砲台用北非土砲與法國早年贈給貝伊的克農後膛砲組成，那批砲在一八八一年仍屬法國軍械；加貝斯五座砲台則是在英國工程技術協助下新造的，配一八八一年新裝的後膛線膛砲，與突尼斯的小型近岸蒸汽船一起守住那個港口。陸軍方面，法軍是一八七四年式步槍、七厘米與八十毫米野戰砲，外加駱駝隊；突尼斯的真主之軍仍是舊式燧發火槍配北非土砲，加上地方豪紳的民兵武器。火藥、煤炭與糧食靠海運，內陸全靠駱駝與驛馬，決定這場戰爭節奏的，是封鎖線與補給距離，而不是砲的射程。
kitsEn: The weapon on the card is a wooden-hulled ship sheathed in iron, a type settled in 1862; the British turn of the gun turret away from the armour began with ships of this kind. Yet in the Tunisian bay in 1881 the guns that actually fired were French flatironclad gunboats, the Milan and the Tage, two low-built gunboats built around 1870 that swept the deck with two large breech-loading guns each and stood in the front at both the action off Bizerte and the bombardment off Gabès; the wooden ironclads that had been the French battle line were by then mostly in reserve or under refit, and the cruisers La Naïque, Héros and Montségur, with a number of torpedo gunboats and gunboats, carried the blockade line and the scouting. The heaviest blood of the ironclad was on show in the Italian detachment: the French-built wooden ironclads Carlo Alberto and Enrico Dandolo, together with the Audace built by the Samuda brothers yard in England, entered the roads of Tunis in the spring and summer of 1881 as a demonstration, not as a fighting force. The defensive artillery was the exact opposite. The batteries at Bizerte and La Goulette mixed North African bronze pieces with Krupp breech-loading guns that France had given to the Bey in earlier years, guns that in 1881 still belonged to the French ordnance; the five batteries at Gabès were newly built with British engineering assistance, armed with rifled breech-loading pieces fitted in 1881, and together with the small Tunisian coastal steamers they held that harbour. On land the French carried the Model 1874 rifle, seven-centimetre and eighty-millimetre field guns, and camel trains, while the Djund of Tunis still had old flintlock muskets with North African pieces, added to the weapons of the notables' militias. Gunpowder, coal and provisions came in by sea and inland everything moved on camels and pack animals, which means the rhythm of this war was set by the blockade line and the distances of supply, not by the range of the guns.
tactics: 這場戰爭的樣板是先封海，再上岸，最後用海軍餵養遠征：分艦隊先切斷突尼斯的對外航線，把貝伊的南部據點各自孤立，再用陸軍沿南北幾條大道推上去。海上只有兩次真正的炮擊，但兩次都定調。一八八一年五月十二日至十四日的比斯克拉之役最有名：法軍艦隊駛入比斯克拉錨地，突尼斯岸防砲先開火，法軍以米蘭號與塔日號的平鐵甲砲艇回擊，雙方對射數小時，突尼斯砲台受損，法軍損失輕微，貝伊政府從此明白海岸不再是自己的。一八八一年十二月二十六日的加貝斯砲擊最狠：法國艦隊在外海展開，逼近到近距離逐座砲擊，五座砲台被毀三座，突尼斯守軍約二百人陣亡、五百人受傷，港內汽船被毀或被俘，十二月二十八日加貝斯被封鎖，次年一月法軍才進城。陸上則是一連串短促的推進與掃蕩：六月法軍由突尼斯城沿海岸公路南下攻斯法克斯，艦隊在側翼提供火力掩護，突尼斯守軍一觸即潰；十月起薩赫勒地區爆發反抗，義軍切斷驛路、襲擊哨所，法軍以縱隊掃過村落，奪下反軍的堡寨，再以駱駝隊與輕便鐵路把南部據點串起來；核心原則只有一條：不讓貝伊的軍隊重新集中，也不讓部落的武裝取得彈藥。
tacticsEn: The pattern of this war was to seal the sea first, land second, and then feed the advance from the fleet. The squadron cut off the outward shipping of Tunisia, so that each of the Bey's southern positions was isolated on its own, and the army then pushed up the few roads running north and south. At sea there were only two real bombardments, but both set the tone. The action of Bizerte, from 12 to 14 May 1881, is the better known: the French squadron steamed into the Bizerte roads, the Tunisian shore batteries opened fire first, and the French answered with the flatironclad gunboats Milan and Tage. The two sides exchanged fire for several hours, the Tunisian batteries were damaged, the French lost little, and the Bey's government understood from that day that the coast was no longer its own. The bombardment of Gabès on 26 December 1881 was the harsher. The French squadron deployed outside the harbour and closed to short range to batter the forts one by one; three of the five batteries were destroyed, the Tunisian garrison lost about two hundred dead and five hundred wounded, the steamers in the harbour were sunk or captured, and Gabès was blockaded on 28 December. Only in January 1882 did the French enter the town. On land came a succession of short pushes and sweeps: in June the French marched south from Tunis along the coastal road against Sfax with the squadron covering the flank, and the Tunisian garrison gave way at the first contact; from October the Sahel rose in revolt, the insurgents cut the caravan roads and raided outposts, the French swept through the villages in column, took the insurgent strongholds, and then knitted the southern posts together with camel trains and a light railway. The single governing principle was this: never allow the Bey's troops to concentrate again, and never allow the tribal armament to obtain ammunition.
data: 可核對的數字大致如下。法軍在突尼斯的兵力，最初是一八八一年五月十四日登陸的三個營，約三千人；到一八八二年三月增到八千人，五月再增至約二萬五千人。突尼斯一方的常備軍，在一八七〇年代裁減後約三千人，加上手民兵與部落武裝數千不等；法國使團在戰前的報告裡估計貝伊能調動的兵力在五千上下。海上，法國分艦隊出動的戰艦約二十艘，義大利則派出三艘木殼鐵甲艦示威。日期線清楚：1881年3月30日義大利代表多西在國會演說，4月9日《陳情書》事件，4月28日法國向貝伊提出最後通牒，5月12日《巴爾多條約》簽訂、同日海軍抵達突尼斯港，5月14日法軍登陸，5月26日法國對烏里瑪與豪紳下最後通牒，6月5日被捕者被押往西西里附近的拉加利特島，12月26日加貝斯砲擊、12月28日封鎖，1882年1月法軍進入加貝斯，4月法軍推進到利比亞南部的拉達梅斯綠洲、引發義大利的最後通牒後撤回，5月15日加貝斯的蓋·塔哈爾被處決。封鎖的代價也有數字：1870年至1881年間進入突尼斯港口而被扣押的英國商船約四十六艘，英方估計損失逾十二萬英鎊，事件最終在外交層面低調收場。加貝斯一役的砲擊消耗以千計發計。
dataEn: The figures that can be checked run roughly as follows. The French force in Tunisia was at first the three battalions that landed on 14 May 1881, about three thousand men; it rose to eight thousand by March 1882 and to some twenty-five thousand by May. The regular army of Tunis, after the cuts of the 1870s, was about three thousand strong, with militia and tribal armament numbering several thousand more; the French mission estimated before the war that the Bey could bring perhaps five thousand men into the field. At sea the French squadron put about twenty war vessels into the operation, while Italy sent three wooden ironclads as a display of force. The sequence of dates is clear: 30 March 1881, the speech of the Italian consul Dossi in parliament; 9 April, the episode of the cahier de doléances; 28 April, the French ultimatum to the Bey; 12 May, the signature of the Bardo Treaty and the arrival of the fleet in the roads of Tunis; 14 May, the French landing; 26 May, the second ultimatum, this time to the ulema and the notables; 5 June, the prisoners shipped off to the island of La Galite off Sicily; 26 December, the bombardment of Gabès, and on 28 December the blockade; January 1882, the French entry into Gabès; April, the French advance to the oasis of Rhadames in southern Libya, and the withdrawal after the Italian ultimatum; 15 May, the execution of G. Tahar at Gabès. The blockade has its own figures: about forty-six British merchant vessels that entered Tunisian ports between 1870 and 1881 were detained, the British estimating their losses at more than one hundred and twenty thousand pounds sterling, and the matter was closed quietly at the diplomatic level. The expenditure of shells at Gabès is counted in thousands.
cause: 打起來的原因分三層。最深的一層是突尼斯的命運早已被瓜分：一八七四年《拉馬丹條約》之後，突尼斯的關稅與稅收交由國際金融委員會接管，貝伊的財政權被削去一大半；法國要的正是最後一步——在突尼斯駐兵並接管外交。直接引線是一八八〇至八一年的一系列摩擦：法國想把一條通往阿爾及利亞方向、加爾達伊亞一線的鐵路特許權拿到手，貝伊的宮廷與烏里瑪為此爭執不休；一八七九年法國派任常駐代表後，摩擦從特許權升級到主權；意大利一方在三月三十日多西的國會演說中把法國的做法說成是對一個伊斯蘭國家的侮辱，義大利的鐵甲艦分隊隨即駛向突尼斯港；第三層是純粹的軍事判斷：法國情報認定突尼斯的烏里瑪與利比亞的賽努西教團有聯繫，一旦起義成形，突尼斯、的黎波里與阿爾及利亞三地同時點火，貝伊的軍隊便會從背後起來。於是四月二十八日的最後通牒先給貝伊、二十六日的第二道給烏里瑪，五月十二日條約簽訂、五月十四日法軍上岸，事情就這樣在兩個星期裡定案。背後還有更大的一層國際算盤：英國要在通往印度的路上先解決埃及，法國則要趕在俄國與德國伸手之前把北非這一段拿穩，倫敦雖有反對聲音，卻默許巴黎先行。
causeEn: There were three layers of cause. The deepest is that the fate of Tunis had already been divided up: after the Treaty of the Ramadan in 1874 the customs and taxes of the country were handed to the international financial commission, and most of the Bey's financial power was taken away; what France wanted was the final step, troops on the ground in Tunis and control of its foreign relations. The immediate fuse was a run of frictions in 1880 and 1881. France wanted the concession for a railway line running towards the Algerian frontier and Ghardaïa, and the Bey's court and the ulema argued endlessly over it; after France appointed a resident in 1879 the friction rose from a concession dispute to a question of sovereignty; and on the Italian side the consul Dossi, in his parliamentary speech of 30 March, described what France was doing as an insult to a Muslim country, whereupon the Italian ironclad squadron steamed towards the roads of Tunis. The third layer was a plain military judgement: French intelligence believed the ulema of Tunis were in contact with the Sanusiyya of Libya, and if a revolt took shape, Tunis, Tripoli and Algeria would flare at once and the Bey's troops would rise from behind. Hence the ultimatum of 28 April to the Bey and the second of 26 May to the ulema, the treaty signed on 12 May and the French ashore on 14 May: the whole thing was settled inside two weeks. Behind it lay a larger international calculation as well. Britain wanted Egypt settled first on the road to India, and France wanted its stretch of North Africa closed off before Russia and Germany reached for it; London objected in words but let Paris go first.
impact: 後果從當年一直排到二十世紀中葉。就突尼斯本身，1881年之後貝伊保住了王位，卻再也不能決定外交、財政與軍隊；法國用常駐總督、法國軍官和國際金融委員會三件套管住了這個行省，烏里瑪的反抗被驅逐到境外，這條斷裂線一直延續：本世紀三十年代，賽努西教團有關的人於1935年9月9日在突尼斯城刺殺法國政要皮埃爾-艾蒂安·弗蘭丹與同伴，兇手被移交後遭當局處決，歐洲列強再度緊張；1952年底武裝鬥爭在突尼斯城街頭打響，1956年3月9日突尼斯宣布獨立，1957年3月6日承認完全獨立，同年七月廢黜貝伊。就海軍而言，法國在1881年占下比斯克拉，等於在地中海上拿到第二個永久軍港，1943年盟軍在北非登陸時它又被用作後勤港口，那面法國三色旗在此懸到1961年比斯克拉危機、1963年法軍最後撤出為止，前後八十二年。就義大利而言，1881年被排除在突尼斯之外，1882年4月拉達梅斯危機幾乎讓兩國開火，這份羞辱記了一百三十年，最終在1911年義大利對突尼斯宣戰、1912年占領該國時償還。
impactEn: The consequences run from that year right into the middle of the twentieth century. For Tunisia itself, after 1881 the Bey kept his throne but could no longer decide foreign policy, finance or the army; France held the province with three instruments, the resident-general, French officers and the international financial commission, and the resistance of the ulema was exiled abroad. That rupture line runs on to the present: in 1935, on 9 September, men connected with the Sanusiyya assassinated the French politician Pierre-Étienne Flandin and his companions in the city of Tunis, and the assassins, handed over, were executed by the authorities, and Europe was tense again; at the end of 1952 armed struggle began in the streets of Tunis; Tunisia declared independence on 9 March 1956, full independence was recognised on 6 March 1957, and the Bey was deposed that July. For the navy, taking Bizerte in 1881 gave France a second permanent base on the Mediterranean; the port served again as a supply harbour for the Allied landings in North Africa in 1943, and the tricolour flown there lasted until the Bizerte crisis of 1961 and the final French withdrawal in 1963, eighty-two years in all. For Italy, exclusion from Tunis in 1881 and the Rhadames crisis of April 1882, which very nearly brought the two countries to war, left a grievance remembered for a hundred and thirty years, and it was paid off when Italy declared war on Tunisia in 1911 and occupied the country in 1912.
result: 結果是法國在八個星期內把突尼斯的抵抗壓成地下活動。法軍登陸後，貝伊的真主之軍被解散，只留一千人的宮廷衛兵；四月末請願反對的烏里瑪與豪紳在六月被押上船，送往西西里附近的拉加利特島，哈達德·本·穆罕默德其後被流放到的黎波里，一八八二年二月死在那裡。地面抵抗在斯法克斯與加貝斯兩地最硬：加貝斯五座砲台在十二月二十六日被法艦打掉三座，守軍死傷慘重，港區被封鎖，法軍一八八二年一月進城；同時法軍在南部沿公路修築一系列據點，把突尼斯與的黎波里邊境連成一道線，1882年5月15日在加貝斯處決了地方抵抗領袖蓋·塔哈爾。國際上，法國在四月推進到拉達梅斯後迫於義大利的最後通牒撤回，暫時收手，但並沒有放棄突尼斯。這場戰爭在軍事上毫無疑問是法國的全面勝利，在政治上卻留下一場打了七十五年的殖民戰爭：貝伊的宮廷成了法國的行政機關，烏里瑪成了反對運動的源頭，比斯克拉成了法國的地中海軍港，而它的收場，誰也想不到是在1963年法國的最後一批軍艦離開那個港口。
resultEn: The result was that within eight weeks France pushed the resistance in Tunis underground. After the landing the Djund of the Bey was disbanded, leaving only a thousand men of the palace guard; the ulema and notables who had petitioned against the protectorate in late April were put on board ship in June and sent to the island of La Galite off Sicily, while Haddad ben Mohamed was deported to Tripoli, where he died in February 1882. The hardest ground resistance was at Sfax and Gabès. Three of the five batteries at Gabès were knocked out by the French ships on 26 December, the garrison was badly hit, the harbour was blockaded, and the French entered the town in January 1882; at the same time the French built a chain of posts along the southern roads, linking the Tunisian frontier to the Tripolitanian one, and on 15 May 1882 they executed the local resistance leader G. Tahar at Gabès. Internationally, France had reached Rhadames in April and then withdrew before the Italian ultimatum, holding its position for the moment without giving up Tunis. Militarily the war was an unambiguous French victory; politically it opened a colonial struggle that would run for seventy-five years. The Bey's palace became an administrative organ of France, the ulema became the fountainhead of the opposition, Bizerte became the French Mediterranean naval base, and the ending nobody would have predicted: in 1963, when the last French warships left that harbour.
